description: With the eye of knowledge (jñāna-cakṣus) one knows the difference between the field and its knower (13.35). The deluded do not see the living being as it departs, stays or enjoys joined with the guṇas; those with the eye of knowledge see it; striving yogins see it established in themselves, while those who have not made themselves ready do not see it even though they strive (15.10–11).

description: The seeing that the text calls true seeing ('he sees'): the supreme lord standing the same in all beings, not perishing among the perishing (13.28); the lord equally present everywhere, so that one does not harm oneself and goes to the highest goal (13.29); actions done by prakṛti alone and one's self as not the doer (13.30); the separate existence of beings as resting in the one and spreading out from it — then one attains brahman (13.31). (Edition numbering; vulgate 13.27–30.)

description: When illumination — knowledge — arises at all the gates of the body, sattva has increased; greed, activity, undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving arise when rajas has increased; absence of illumination, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion when tamas has increased (BhG 14.11–13).

description: Asked for the marks (liṅga) of one gone beyond the guṇas (14.21): he does not hate illumination, activity or delusion when they arise nor long for them when they cease; sits as one indifferent, unshaken by the guṇas, knowing 'the guṇas operate', and does not waver; is alike in pain and pleasure, abiding in himself, the same toward clod, stone and gold, pleasant and unpleasant, blame and praise of himself, honour and dishonour, friend and foe; relinquishes all undertakings (BhG 14.22–25).
